title: Interleaved Sequence Fuzz Runner with KV-cache Checkpointing and Sample Weighting
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: intermittent microbursts and KV-cache invalidation were causing non-deterministic p95 regressions in our seq-mix benchmarks. This PR introduces a new benchmark harness, the Interleaved Sequence Fuzz Runner, that generates correlated interleaved request sequences with configurable sample weights and interleaving patterns, plus a lightweight KV-cache checkpointing layer to exercise cache hits/misses deterministically with replay. Design: the runner composes three primitives: a sequence fuzzer (pattern generator with Markov-backed probability matrices), an interleaver (controls request interleaving and overlap window), and a sampler that attaches weights to sequences to reproduce real-world token distribution skew. The KV-cache checkpointing records and replays KV cache state at configurable checkpoints so we can deterministically reproduce cache-dependent tail latency. Implementation: new binary 'seq-fuzz-runner' under tools/bench, modular Go code with an external JSON workload spec (examples/seq-fuzz-specs/), and a small Python reporting adaptor that converts run traces into the benchmark-lab event schema. This PR includes: - deterministic checkpoint format (binary v1) and migration shim - sample-weighted scheduler that supports per-sequence and per-token weights - interleaving modes: round-robin, burst, poisson-mix - an end-to-end example and README with tuning knobs and cost/perf tradeoffs - integration with existing runner harness and the aggregate reporter API See linked Linear tickets ENG-1492 and ENG-1510 for acceptance criteria. Checklist: [x] unit tests for sequence generator [x] end-to-end local replay mode [x] CI benchmark job updated [x] docs/examples added [ ] optional: add GPU-backed synthetic mode in a follow-up Notes: the description contains no sensitive data. The runner is intended to replace ad-hoc scripts used in perf investigations and to power more reproducible p99/p999 profiling runs. For reproducibility, add --seed flag and deterministic KV checkpointing. Related: this ties into the profiling baselines work for stable-region detection. Performance summary from local runs: median p95 improved in synthetic replay by 0-2ms under light load; under heavy interleaving we observe increased dispatch jitter which our scheduler telemetry now captures (new metrics: seq_fuzz.interleave_jitter_seconds, seq_fuzz.kvcache_hit_ratio).

release_notes: Introduces a reproducible interleaved sequence fuzz runner and KV-cache checkpointing to improve determinism in cache-sensitive perf tests. Adds new metrics seq_fuzz.interleave_jitter_seconds and seq_fuzz.kvcache_hit_ratio. Example specs and CI job included.
